blocks.text: CT-P43 (ustekinumab- stba) is a recombinant human IgG1 directed against the shared p40 subunit of IL-23 and IL-12 cytokines. It is a proposed interchangeable biosimilar to US-Stelara for the same indications as USStelara including moderate to severe PsO, PsA, CD and UC. Ustekinumab binds to the p40 subunits of IL-12 and IL-23, blocking IL-12 and IL-23 from binding to the shared IL-12 receptor subunit beta 1; thereby, disrupting IL12 and IL-23 mediated signaling events and cytokine cascades. Potency of CT-P43 is controlled using a cell-based assay that monitors inhibition of IL12 mediated signaling during drug substance (DS) and drug product (DP) release and stability testing. Ustekinumab binds to the shared P40 subunit of IL-12 or IL-23 and is unable to bind to the IL-12 or IL-23 molecule already bound to its receptor complex, and thus is not likely to mediate Fc effector functions.

blocks.text: CT-P43 is a recombinant human IgG1 directed against the shared p40 subunit of IL-23 and IL-12 cytokines. It is a proposed interchangeable biosimilar to US-Stelara for the same indications as US-Stelara including moderate to severe PsO, PsA, CD and UC. Ustekinumab binds to the p40 subunits of IL-12 and IL-23, blocking IL-12 and IL-23 from binding to the shared IL-12 receptor subunit beta 1; thereby, disrupting IL-12 and IL-23 mediated signaling events and cytokine cascades. Potency of CT-P43 is controlled using a cell-based assay that monitors inhibition of IL-12 mediated signaling during drug substance (DS) and drug product (DP) release and stability testing. Ustekinumab binds to the shared P40 subunit of IL-12 or IL-23 and is unable to bind to the IL-12 or IL-23 molecule already bound to its receptor complex, and thus is not likely to mediate Fc effector functions.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Celltrion is seeking licensure of CT-P43 as an interchangeable biosimilar to U.S.- licensed Stelara (referred to hereafter as US-Stelara) for these strengths and presentations: 90 mg/1.0 mL (90 mg/mL) and 45 mg/0.5 mL (90 mg/mL) in a singledose prefilled syringe (PFS) with safety guard for subcutaneous injection, and 130 mg/26 mL (5 mg/mL) in a single-dose vial for intravenous infusion. These are the same strengths currently available for US-Stelara.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: To support a demonstration that CT-P43 is highly similar to US- Stelara and establish the analytical component of the scientific bridge, Celltrion performed a three-way comparative analytical assessment (CAA). The first sub-study compared the PFS presentations based on the following data:
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: 10 lots of US-Stelara (7 lots of 45 mg/0.5 mL PFS, 3 lots of 90 mg/1.0 mL PFS) with expiration dates ranging from April 2023 through September 2024;
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: 10 lots of E.U.-approved-Stelara (EU-Stelara) (8 lots of 45 mg/0.5 mL PFS, 2 lots of 90 mg/1.0 mL PFS) with expiration dates ranging from March 2023 through October 2024;
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: 6 lots of CT-P43 PFS drug product (DP) (4 lots of 45 mg/0.5 mL PFS, 2 lots of 90 mg/1.0 mL PFS,) manufactured between April 2020 and May 2022 from 6 independent CT-P43 DS lots.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: For several assays not expected to be impacted by the DP manufacturing process, independent CT-P43 drug substance (DS) lots were included in the CAA if a DP lot manufactured from that DS lot was not available at the time of the assessment. Up to 4 DS lots manufactured between January 2020 and August 2021 were used in the final CAA.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In addition, Celltrion also performed a second comparative analytical assessment substudy between CT-P43 and US-Stelara for the 130 mg/26 mL vial using the following:
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: 6 lots of US-Stelara (130 mg/26 mL vial) with expiration dates ranging from June 2023 through July 2025. For assessment of protein concentration only, an additional 5 lots of US-Stelara were used for a total of 11 lots.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: 6 lots of CT-P43 130 mg/26 mL vial DP manufactured between December 2020 and April 2023 from the same 6 independent CT-P43 DS lots also used for in the manufacturing of 6 CT-P43 PFS drug product lots already included in the above CAA sub-study.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The DP lots used in clinical studies and the CT-P43 PPQ lots for all strengths are included in the CAA. The ages of US-Stelara and EU-Stelara at the time of testing were adequate to capture potential differences or variability over time for US-Stelara and EUStelara.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: The CAA included comparison of physicochemical and functional quality attributes (QAs) of CT-P43, US-Stelara and EU-Stelara using orthogonal methods, as well as comparison of their degradation profiles under forced degradation conditions. The CAA included a 3-way comparative assessment between the PFS presentations only since this presentation was used in the clinical studies and 2-way comparative assessment between the 130 mg/26 mL vials with the same methods. In addition, the Applicant conducted a comparability assessment between CT-P43 45 mg/0.5 mL SC PFS and CT-P43 IV 130 mg/26 mL vial DP and the data support that these are analytically comparable. Results from method validation or qualification studies support the suitability of the methods used in the analytical assessment. The Applicant used a criticality-based data analysis approach to evaluate the analytical results that was consistent with FDA recommendations. The approach included the following: QAs amenable to statistical analysis were compared to quality ranges (QRs) of mean ± 2 (very high criticality) or 3 (high and moderate criticality) * standard deviations (SD)) established from US-Stelara and EU-Stelara. In addition, for certain low criticality attributes, results are evaluated against the min-max ranges of US-Stelara and EUStelara to support similarity. If a result exceeded the min-max range, the magnitude and the criticality of the observed differences were discussed and justified. QAs not amenable to quantitative analysis or otherwise justified were analyzed by a qualitative comparison (e.g. visual comparison,). DP vial samples used in the 2-way CAA substudy included non-independent DS lots from those used in the 3-way CAA sub-study; however quality attributes that could be impacted by the DP manufacturing process and difference in formulation were assessed using an adequate number of DP lots.

blocks.text: For the comparative stability studies, the Applicant conducted studies under forced degradation conditions (thermal stress at 55°C for up to 6 days, photo stress, oxidation and hydrolytic degradation). The comparative forced degradation studies show similar degradation pathways and degradation rate among CT-P43, US-Stelara and EUStelara.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Our assessment of the CT-P43 and US-Stelara comparative analytical data supports the determination that CT-P43 is highly similar to US-Stelara, notwithstanding minor differences in clinically inactive components. CT-P43 has the same strengths, dosage form and routes of administration as US-Stelara. The Applicant used a comprehensive set of analytical methods that were suitable to evaluate the critical quality attributes of CT-P43 and US-Stelara to support the demonstration that the products are highly similar. The number of lots tested and data analysis approaches used were appropriate or justified as needed to allow for a meaningful evaluation of the results of the analytical studies. The differences observed in a subset of the quality attributes do not preclude a determination that CT-P43 and US-Stelara are highly similar.
blocks.speaker: regulator

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: In addition, Celltrion used three-way pairwise comparisons of CT-P43, US-Stelara, and EU-Stelara to establish the analytical component of the scientific bridge between CTP43, US-Stelara, and EU-Stelara to support the relevance of the data generated from clinical studies using EU-Stelara as the comparator in the assessment of biosimilarity. Our assessment of the data supports that the Applicant established the analytical component of the scientific bridge between CT-P43, US-Stelara, and EU-Stelara, using the same methods and statistical approaches used to evaluate that CT-P43 is highly similar to US-Stelara. This supports the relevance of the data generated from clinical studies using EU-Stelara as the comparator for the assessment of biosimilarity.

blocks.text: CT-P43 is a recombinant human IgG1 directed against the shared p40 subunit of IL-23 and IL-12 cytokines. It is a proposed interchangeable biosimilar to US-Stelara for the same indications as US-Stelara including moderate to severe PsO, PsA, CD and UC. Ustekinumab binds to the p40 subunits of IL-12 and IL-23, blocking IL-12 and IL-23 from binding to the shared IL-12 receptor subunit beta 1; thereby, disrupting IL-12 and IL-23 mediated signaling events and cytokine cascades. Potency of CT-P43 is controlled using a cell-based assay that monitors inhibition of IL-12 mediated signaling during drug substance (DS) and drug product (DP) release and stability testing. Ustekinumab binds to the shared P40 subunit of IL-12 or IL-23 and is unable to bind to the IL-12 or IL-23 molecule already bound to its receptor complex, and thus is not likely to mediate Fc effector functions.

blocks.text: Our assessment of the CT-P43 and US-Stelara comparative analytical data supports the determination that CT-P43 is highly similar to US-Stelara, notwithstanding minor differences in clinically inactive components. The Applicant used a comprehensive set of analytical methods that were suitable to evaluate the critical quality attributes of CT-P43 and US-Stelara to support the demonstration that the products are highly similar. The number of lots tested and data analysis approaches used were appropriate or justified as needed to allow for a meaningful evaluation of the results of the analytical studies. The differences observed in a subset of the quality attributes do not preclude a determination that CT-P43 and US-Stelara are highly similar.

In addition, C-lysine truncation occurs readily in vivo; therefore, the differences are not expected to impact PK and safety. The IEC-HPLC results for CT-P43, U.S.-Stelara, and E.U.-Stelara before enzymatic treatments show lower levels of acidic species and lower levels of basic species for CT-P43.
